data.long_meaning: Derived from the Sanskrit word ‘chitra’ meaning ‘art’, ‘picture’, or ‘sketch’. In Hindu mythology, Chitral is a female name associated with creativity and artistic expression. The name Chitral carries the meaning “Art, Picture, Sketch” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Chitral usually hope their child will grow to embody art, picture, sketch and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.etymology: Chitral belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Art, Picture, Sketch.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Chitral total 8, giving a life-path number of 8. Number 8 is linked with Saturn and with the qualities of ambition, resilience and material success.

data.cultural_impact: The name Chitral holds significant cultural value within the Hindu community, as it is derived from the Sanskrit word ‘chitra’, which holds symbolic meaning as ‘art’, ‘picture’, or ‘sketch’. Artistic expression is a fundamental aspect of Hindu culture and beliefs, often depicted through various forms of art such as painting, sculpture, dance, and literature. By bestowing a child with this name, parents may be passing on a legacy of creativity and artistic expression, inspiring them to explore their own talents and contribute to the rich artistic traditions of their community.
data.spiritual_significance: In Hindu mythology, the name Chitral embodies the feminine aspect of creativity and artistic expression, reflecting the inherent connection between the divine and human creative processes. It is believed that the divine power of creativity transcends the physical world and manifests through the artistic creations of humankind. Therefore, choosing the name Chitral for a child underscores the belief that the child will carry the divine spark of creativity within them and is encouraged to foster this gift throughout their life, as an expression of the divine and a means of personal growth and spiritual realization.
